blogs.title: Beyond the Bite: Recognizing Capnocytophaga Sepsis in the ED
blogs.description: Dog bites are common, but Capnocytophaga canimorsus sepsis is uncommon and deadly. This post reviews who is at risk (including immunocompetent hosts), clinical cues that should trigger early broad-spectrum coverage (hypoglycemia, leukopenia, DIC, acral ischemia), and pragmatic empiric choices for severe presentations (e.g., piperacillin/tazobactam or a carbapenem; amoxicillin–clavulanate for outpatient prophylaxis). We also discuss culture delays with this fastidious organism, the growing role of rapid molecular diagnostics, and practical strategies to avoid under-triage when qSOFA underestimates severity.

blogs.title: When DIC Isn’t the Whole Story: Unmasking CM-HUS After Sepsis
blogs.description: Sepsis-associated DIC can obscure a superimposed thrombotic microangiopathy. This case illustrates the red flags for complement-mediated HUS (CM-HUS): late-onset hemolysis after initial stabilization, persistent thrombocytopenia, rising LDH with undetectable haptoglobin, and a smear rich in schistocytes. We’ll cover when to pivot from a DIC-centric framework, the value and timing of kidney biopsy, and how to build a monitoring plan that catches evolving TMA before irreversible renal injury.

blogs.title: TMA on the Clock: PLASMIC, ADAMTS13, and the Bridge to the Right Therapy
blogs.description: Early differentiation of TTP, STEC-HUS, and CM-HUS changes lives. We outline a rapid, stepwise approach: use PLASMIC to triage, send ADAMTS13 urgently, rule out STEC with stool PCR, and start plasma exchange when TTP is possible—then de-escalate if ADAMTS13 is >10%. We discuss when to initiate eculizumab, how to time it relative to PEX, and the role of biopsy in consolidating the diagnosis when platelets begin to recover.

blogs.title: Eculizumab in the Hot Zone: Starting Complement Blockade Around Active Infection
blogs.description: Complement inhibition saves kidneys in CM-HUS but increases vulnerability to encapsulated organisms, including Neisseria and potentially Capnocytophaga. This post walks through timing eculizumab initiation (ideally after bacteremia clears), vaccine logistics (MenACWY and MenB, preferably ≥2 weeks pre-treatment), and antibiotic prophylaxis when therapy can’t wait. We cover regimen choices, duration during ongoing blockade, and bedside tactics to mitigate infectious risk while not delaying organ-saving therapy.

blogs.title: The Misleading Coombs: Drug-Related DAT Positivity and Hemolysis Pitfalls
blogs.description: A positive DAT can anchor clinicians on autoimmune hemolysis, but transfusions and beta-lactams can cause false positives. We review a practical hemolysis workup in the critically ill: interpreting DAT in context, reconciling reticulocyte responses under marrow stress, and prioritizing the smear (schistocytes) and hemolysis labs over DAT alone. Case-based pearls help avoid corticosteroid overuse and redirect toward TMA when MAHA is the dominant signal.

blogs.title: Normal C3, Sick Kidneys: Getting Complement Testing Right in Suspected CM-HUS
blogs.description: Normal C3/C4 doesn’t exclude CM-HUS. We detail which assays help (AH50/CH50, factor H/I/B, anti–factor H antibodies) and how PEX and eculizumab distort results. Practical tips: draw a complement and genetics panel before PEX/therapy when feasible, understand the limited yield and delayed turnaround of genetic testing, and use clinical trajectory to guide duration of eculizumab in infection-triggered cases without pathogenic variants.
